Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system

Class TorPrivateMode

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.TorPrivateMode
public final class TorPrivateMode extends Object
The desktop-wide Private (Tor) mode: a Whonix-style anonymity guarantee expressed at the desktop level rather than the OS level. While the mode is on, every network client the desktop owns is forced through the local tor SOCKS endpoint, and a daemon monitor watches the tor daemon: the moment it stops, the mode trips to TorPrivateMode.State.CUT and raises NetworkCut, so a broken guarantee degrades to a loud, refused network - never to a silent clearnet leak.

Enforcement is by construction, not by promise:

  • JVM clients (the web browser, java.net.http, URLConnection) ride the SOCKS system properties installed by enable() plus a default ProxySelector; SOCKS v5 resolves names remotely, so DNS leaks through the resolver too.
  • External commands the desktop spawns receive the matching *_proxy environment variables (proxyEnv(boolean, int)), so proxy-respecting children follow the same path.
  • When tor dies the SOCKS endpoint dies with it: every forced socket attempt is refused. The TorPrivateMode.State.CUT flag additionally lets UIs abort early and explain why.

Tor remains a plain service: its lifecycle is still delegated to PrivacyService (and through it the system-management-contract.md §4.1 init abstraction), so this class adds no tor-specific service handling - only the anonymity guarantee on top. The mutating start is polkit-escalated and MUST be confirmed by the calling UI before enable() is invoked (§4.7).

Every decision is pure and headless-testable: transition(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.TorPrivateMode.State, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.TorPrivateMode.Event), monitorTick(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.TorPrivateMode.State, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.PrivacyService.TorState), proxyProperties(int), proxyEnv(boolean, int), parseTorCheck(java.lang.String) and socksPort() touch no process and no global state. The live enable()/disable()/monitor wrap them.

  • Method Details

    • transition

      public static TorPrivateMode.State transition(TorPrivateMode.State current, TorPrivateMode.Event event)
      The state transition table. Unknown/null inputs are tolerated: a null event leaves the state untouched, a null state reads as TorPrivateMode.State.OFF.

    • monitorTick

      public static TorPrivateMode.State monitorTick(TorPrivateMode.State current, PrivacyService.TorState tor)
      One monitor tick: the observed tor state against the current mode state. TorPrivateMode.State.ON with tor not running trips to TorPrivateMode.State.CUT (the kill switch); TorPrivateMode.State.CUT with tor running again recovers to TorPrivateMode.State.ON. Every other combination is a no-op. Fails closed: an UNKNOWN tor state cuts just like STOPPED.

    • proxyProperties

      public static Map<String,String> proxyProperties(int port)
      The JVM SOCKS enforcement properties for port: the host, the port and a non-proxy list limited to loopback, so nothing else bypasses the proxy. Pure; enable() installs exactly this map.

    • proxyEnv

      public static Map<String,String> proxyEnv(boolean on, int port)
      The environment variables a spawned child process must carry while the mode is on (socks5h = remote DNS through the proxy). Empty when on is false, so callers can putAll unconditionally.

    • socksPort

      public static int socksPort()
      The effective SOCKS port: the "lg.tor.socksPort" system property when it parses to a valid port, else DEFAULT_SOCKS_PORT.

    • parseTorCheck

      public static TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict parseTorCheck(String body)
      Parses the tor-project check body ({"IsTor":true,...}) into a TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict. Fails closed: a blank/null body is TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict.UNREACHABLE, anything reachable that does not positively confirm tor is TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict.NOT_TOR.

    • enable

      public static boolean enable()
      Enters private mode: probes tor, starts it through PrivacyService when stopped (polkit-escalated - the caller MUST have confirmed first), installs the SOCKS enforcement and starts the monitor. Idempotent while TorPrivateMode.State.ON; from TorPrivateMode.State.CUT it retries the tor start and recovers when the daemon is back.
      Returns:
      true if the mode ended up TorPrivateMode.State.ON

    • disable

      public static void disable()
      Leaves private mode from any state: stops the monitor, removes the SOCKS enforcement (restoring the previous ProxySelector) and lowers NetworkCut. Safe to call when already off.

    • leakCheck

      public static TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict leakCheck()
      Verifies the anonymity guarantee end-to-end by asking the tor project's exit-IP check through the proxy only. Never throws; any I/O or protocol failure is TorPrivateMode.LeakVerdict.UNREACHABLE.
